## Development

Development of the Trichy Assault Rifle began in the early 2010s at the Ordnance Factory Tiruchirappalli as part of efforts to create an indigenous 7.62×39mm assault rifle. The initial version, introduced in 2011, involved converting FN FAL receivers to accept 7.62×39mm ammunition and use locally produced magazines. Field trials for this model were conducted, including tests by the Indian Army, with an effective range of 400 meters reported.

In 2015, further development led to a redesigned version based on the Bulgarian AR-M1, featuring a mono-block receiver and modular enhancements. A production line was established in 2017, and the first batch of 200 rifles was delivered to the Chandigarh police in March of that year. The Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) conducted extensive testing in November 2017, firing over 15,000 rounds for lifecycle evaluation and 2,400 rounds for reliability, followed by field trials in early 2018.

In August 2021, a down-folding butt version was launched to facilitate quicker movement during patrols and guard duties, commemorating 75 years of India's independence. This variant addressed requests from Central Armed Police Forces and state police.

## Design

The Trichy Assault Rifle is a gas-operated, selective-fire weapon with a rotating bolt mechanism. It fires in single-shot and burst modes, with some customized versions for police forces limited to single-shot only. The rifle uses a curved 30-round magazine made of fiber-reinforced polymer with steel inserts.

Key specifications include a weight of approximately 3.4 to 3.6 kg, an overall length of 900 mm with the butt extended and 650 mm when folded, an effective range of 350 to 400 meters, and a muzzle velocity of 710 to 715 m/s. It features four-groove rifling and Picatinny rails for mounting optical sights and accessories, including an under-barrel grenade launcher. Tritium sights aid night firing. The design resembles the Bulgarian AR-M1F41, with minor differences in the gas block and cleaning rod, and performs similarly to the AK-103.

The TAR was developed for counter-insurgency and counter-terrorism operations, emphasizing lightweight construction and modularity.

## Variants

The Trichy Assault Rifle is available in several configurations:

- **Fixed butt**: Standard version for general use.
- **Side-folding butt**: Allows compact storage.
- **Down-folding butt**: Introduced in 2021 for enhanced portability during patrolling.
- **Telescoping stock**: M4-patterned adjustable stock option.

A compact carbine variant, the TriCa (Trichy Carbine), was launched in July 2021. It weighs 3.17 kg, has an effective range of 150 to 175 meters, and includes a muzzle booster to reduce flash and sound. The TriCa uses the same ammunition and magazines as the TAR and AK-47, making parts interchangeable. It is designed for special forces, helicopter crews, paratroopers, and infantry combat vehicle operators.

## Operators

The Trichy Assault Rifle is primarily used by Indian security forces:

- **Border Security Force (BSF)**: Inducted several hundred units, with an additional 125 rifles procured in 2024 along with bayonets.
- **Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF)**: Ordered 6,167 rifles following successful trials in 2018.
- **Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP)**, **Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB)**, and **Central Industrial Security Force (CISF)**: Procured in significant numbers.
- **State police forces**: Adopted by units in Chandigarh, Kolkata, Kerala, and others under modernization programs.
- **Indian Army**: Proposed for reserve units and tested, though not widely adopted as a primary rifle.

No confirmed exports or foreign operators as of December 2025.

**Demand of TAR among Central Reserved Forces**

TAR or Trichy Assault Rifle is a product from erstwhile Ordinance Factory Trichy and now part of AWEIL. The development of the assault rifle was started in 2015 and a production line was established in 2017. The first batch of 200 TARs were delivered to Chandigarh police in March 2017. In November 2017, the CRPF tested the rifle’s functionality and its reliability. Over 15,000 rounds were fired to test the TAR’s life cycle and over 2,400 rounds to test its reliability. In February 2018, the TAR underwent field trial at Jagdalpur, Raipur, Guwahati and Srinagar. After regressive trials, the CRPF had placed an order for 6167 rifles TAR.

In January 2024, it was reported that BSF is acquiring 125 TAR rifles along with bayonets and other accessories. BSF has experience with operating TAR and has inducted the assault rifle into service earlier. Other Central Armed Police Forces which include SSB, ITBP & CISF has also procured TAR in some significant numbers. Police forces in several states have also inducted TAR under their modernisation scheme.

**TAR : Specifications**

The Trichy Assault Rifle (TAR) is a 7.62X39mm powerful automatic weapon designed to destroy the enemy by fire in single and burst firing mode. It has an effective range of 350m. Its light weight and modular design make it suitable for the counter-insurgency and counter-terror operations. It comes with foldable and fixed butt type, depending upon the requirement. The foldable butt version is helpful in quick and easy movement of personnel in guard and patrolling duty. The overall length of TAR-Down folding butt is 900mm in butt open condition and 650mm in butt folding condition. The rifle weighs 3.4kg and features a curved magazine with 30 rounds.

The rifle has mono-block receiver body & fibre reinforced polymer magazine with steel inserts. It also has a customised version with single round firing mode for police forces. It also features Tritium filled Sources for night firing and picatinny rail for mounting optical sights. It can also be fitted with Under barrel grenade launcher.

TAR very closely resembles Bulgarian Arsenal AR-M1F41. There is minor difference in the gas block & cleaning rod of the assault rifles. There is also some noticeable difference in the pistol grip. TAR is being supplied to paramilitary forces to reduce imports from Bulgaria. The unique feature of TAR is that it provides 12 O’clock rails on upper handguard which is not available in any other AKM copy. TAR is 7.62x39mm assault rifle, similar in calibre to AK-203. In fact TAR is almost equivalent to AK-103 and very close to AK-203 in terms of performance.

4.title: "Trichy" Assault Rifle Gaining Traction Among Indian Law Enforcement
4.description: After field trials and subsequent purchasing of the “Trichy” Assault Rifle (TAR) by the Indian Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF), it is being reported that other Indian Law Enforcement entities are taking an interest in the rifle as well.The 7.62x39mm TAR rifle was initially introduced almost a decade ago but appeared to have seen little success in the form that it first existed in.Essentially it appeared to be converting an FN FAL receiver into 7.62x39mm with internally produced magazines.
4.content:
![Image 1: trichy assault rifle gaining traction among indian law enforcement](https://cdn-fastly.thefirearmblog.com/media/2024/05/19/14566681/trichy-assault-rifle-gaining-traction-among-indian-law-enforcement.jpg?size=720x845&nocrop=1)

After field trials and subsequent purchasing of the “Trichy” Assault Rifle (TAR) by the [Indian Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF)](http://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/Tiruchirapalli/crpf-approves-trichy-assault-rifle-after-tests/article19937479.ece), it is being [reported that other Indian Law Enforcement entities are taking an interest in the rifle as well](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/trichy/crpf-most-likely-to-place-orders-for-trichy-assault-rifle/articleshow/63348542.cms). The [7.62x39mm TAR rifle was initially introduced almost a decade ago](https://www.thefirearmblog.com/blog/2011/03/25/trichy-assault-rifle/) but appeared to have seen little success in the form that it first existed in. Essentially it appeared to be converting an FN FAL receiver into 7.62x39mm with internally produced magazines. The current variant is in fact a copy of the Bulgarian Arsenal 7.62x39mm AR-M1 (milled receiver) with some modifications to the buttstock in a fixed stock, folding stock, and telescoping M4 patterned stock variation. It appears that the latch to secure the right folding stock is left on the receiver even when the fixed and telescoping stocks have been installed. This improved variant was [officially unveiled in March of 2017](http://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/Tiruchirapalli/ordnance-factory-develops-assault-rifle/article17528273.ece), more than a year ago. The name “Trichy” is short for Ordnance Factory Tiruchirappalli where a large number of defense articles are produced, to include the dreaded INSAS.

![Image 2: trichy assault rifle gaining traction among indian law enforcement](https://cdn-fastly.thefirearmblog.com/media/2024/05/19/14566684/trichy-assault-rifle-gaining-traction-among-indian-law-enforcement.jpg?size=720x845&nocrop=1)

![Image 3: trichy assault rifle gaining traction among indian law enforcement](https://cdn-fastly.thefirearmblog.com/media/2024/05/19/14566687/trichy-assault-rifle-gaining-traction-among-indian-law-enforcement.jpg?size=720x845&nocrop=1)

The need for this rifle stems not from the violence in the Kashmir regions but instead the “Red Corridor” along the south eastern portion of the Indian subcontinent where India has a Maoist insurgency ( [in which all INSAS rifles were ordered replaced…](https://www.thefirearmblog.com/blog/2015/05/04/india-replaces-all-insas-rifles-in-red-zones-with-aks-cites-insas-as-defective/)). Interestingly one of the big drives for the adoption of this rifle comes from the workers who make it, insisting on the rifles adoption by Law Enforcement and paramilitary organizations. From The Hindu-

> Approval of TAF is a shot in the arm for the employee unions that had been expressing concern over the decline in manpower at the OFT. Manpower had declined to around 2,000 from about 3,500 10 years ago, V.Balachandran, national executive member of the AIDEF, said.
> 
> 
> The development comes in the backdrop of AIDEF and two other employee unions: INDWF and BPMS which together represent the cause of four lakh employees in 41 ordnance factories in the country, opposing import of AK-47 rifle, and assailing the Centre’s move for introduction of public-private-partnership model.

Looking at India’s [sinking ship of a reliable rifle procurement program](https://www.thefirearmblog.com/blog/2018/02/22/india-announces-purchase-of-small-arms-as-search-for-insas-replacement-continues/), this puts the INSAS debacle in a somewhat new perspective in that it is government workers who insist on continuing with a substandard product in order to keep their jobs. Eerily similar to the M14 debacle out of Springfield Armory in the 1950s, another example of a rifle program that should have been taken more seriously.

[![Image 4: Sweepstsake Banner](https://cdn-fastly.thefirearmblog.com/media/cms/2025/11/12/176297835561280/photo.jpg?size=600x300)](https://www.springfield-armory.com/gear-pac/?utm_source=TFB&utm_medium=Website&utm_campaign=GearPac)

![Image 5: trichy assault rifle gaining traction among indian law enforcement](https://cdn-fastly.thefirearmblog.com/media/2024/05/19/14566690/trichy-assault-rifle-gaining-traction-among-indian-law-enforcement.jpg?size=720x845&nocrop=1)

![Image 6: trichy assault rifle gaining traction among indian law enforcement](https://cdn-fastly.thefirearmblog.com/media/2024/05/19/14566693/trichy-assault-rifle-gaining-traction-among-indian-law-enforcement.jpg?size=720x845&nocrop=1)

During the Trichy factory’s Ordnance Day 2018, the TAR rifle was on display along with numerous other small arms that are made at the factory. Although not featured in this video below, readers can see some of the domestically produced small arms coming from the factory. Note in particular the ground mounted 240 design derivative with what appears to be a nonadjustable and fixed RPD patterned gas port.

Don’t take the video too seriously though, as some of the captions and weapons handling skills are cringe worthy.

6.content:

Launch of 7.62*39mm Trichy Assault Rifle (TAR) Down Folding Butt Version
------------------------------------------------------------------------

 प्रविष्टि तिथि: 26 AUG 2021 12:51PM by PIB Chennai 

In commemoration of 75 years of independence, Ordnance Factory, Tiruchirappalli launched Down folding butt version of 7.62*39mm Trichy Assault Rifle on 25 th August 2021. At present, Ordnance Factory, Tiruchirappali, is manufacturing TAR Rifles in two variants i.e. Fixed butt and side folding butt versions.

The 7.62*39mm Trichy Assault Rifle (TAR) is a powerful individual automatic weapon designed to destroy the enemy by fire in single and burst firing mode. It is a single shot Rifle in normal mode and it can be used in burst mode also. By firing in burst mode in short series, group or single targets at a range up to 500m can be destroyed. However, the destructive effect of the TAR is up to a range of 1350m.

Ordnance Factory, Trichirappallin developed and manufactured TAR Down folding butt version to meet the customer requirement as some of the CAPF units, State Police and RPF required the Down folding butt version for quick and easy movement of personnel in guard and patrolling duty.

The overall length of TAR-Down folding butt is 900mm in butt open condition and 650mm in butt folding condition.

The Down folding butt version of 7.62*39mm Trichy Assault Rifle launched by Shri Sanjay Dwivedi, IOFS, General Manager, Ordnance Factory, Trichirappalli and Shri Rajiv Jain, IOFS, Addl. Kolkata Police are set to phase out their decades-old .303 guns and replace them with modern assault rifles developed by the Ordnance Factory Tiruchirappalli.

The new Trichy Assault Rifles (TAR), modelled on the Bulgarian AR-M1 and described as an indigenous variant of the AK-47, are expected to arrive in batches early next year. “The consignment will reach in phases, and distribution will begin soon after,” an officer of the rank of deputy commissioner of Kolkata Police said.

ADVERTISEMENT

One of the biggest advantages is weight, senior officers said. The old .303 rifles weigh about 5.5kg, while the TAR is at least 2kg lighter.

The officers said the rifle supports both single-shot and burst fire, allowing accurate engagement of targets up to 500 metres. “Its lightweight modular design and foldable butt make it handy, even for guard and patrolling duty,” a senior officer said.

Kolkata Police have been phasing out ageing .303 rifles and replacing them with INSAS and SLRs (Self-Loading Rifles) in the force’s ongoing modernisation drive.

But officers said the shift to TAR reflects the demands of contemporary policing, after the 26/11 Mumbai attack.

“Several central forces, including the BSF and CRPF, have inducted TAR. This is currently the best option for our forces,” a senior officer said.

The TAR has seen been used across the country. Chhattisgarh Police deployed the weapon during anti-Naxalite operations earlier this year, while Rajasthan, Jharkhand, and Madhya Pradesh police forces have also procured it, sources said. In addition to the TAR, Kolkata Police will procure around 200 automatic 9mm 1A pistols from Rifle Factory, Ishapore.

“Non-lethal munitions from the Tear Smoke Unit in Tekanpur, Madhya Pradesh, are also on the upgrade list,” the officer said. Officers across units said such upgrades bolster not just capability but morale.

“If one has to face a barrage of bullets from terrorists or armed criminals, modern firearms are essential. Personnel on the ground feel far more confident when they know they are equipped with the latest weapons,” a southeast division officer of Kolkata Police said.

TRICHY: The Ordnance Factory Tiruchirappalli (OFT) on Thursday launched a new weapon called TriCa (Trichy Carbine), a mini version of the Trichy Assault Rifle (TAR).  
The 7.62 X 39 mm portable weapon launched on the carbine platform was entirely manufactured at the ordnance factory here.  
TriCa weighs 3.17 kg (including the magazine) and is lighter compared to the assault rifles.

![Image 3: 1x1 polls](https://static.toiimg.com/photo/25581306.cms)

It is a compact automatic weapon designed for the crews of infantry combat vehicles, helicopters, paratroopers, state police force and special operation forces.  
OFT sources said that TriCa is equipped with a special muzzle booster to hide the flash and mitigate the sound during the firing. The weapon has an effective range of 150 to 175 metre.  

TriCa can use ammunition and magazines, as well as the interchangeable parts of general assault rifles (TAR and AK-47). The field trials conducted yielded positive results.  
The weapon was launched by Sanjay Dwivedi, IOFS, general manager, OFT.
